 Hon'Ble Jitendra Kumar Sinha, J. 
1. Heard Shri Manish Kumar Dwivedi, learned counsel for the applicants, Shri O.P. Singh, learned
A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2.  The present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime no.234 of 2023,
under Sections 406, 420, 504, 506, 323 of IPC, Police Station Quarsi, District Aligarh, with the prayer that in the event of arrest, applicant may be released on bail.
3. It has been argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that applicants are innocent and they have been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that the case relates to some civil dispute, which has been given colour of criminality.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicants that the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance of the offences under Sections 420,
406 IPC and as per law laid-down in the case of Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. and Others Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 2248 and pointed out that both the offences under Sections 406, 420 IPC can not be applied simultaneously, as they both are antithetical to each other.

entities.text: Delhi Race Club (1940) Ltd. and Others Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Another, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 2248
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the offences alleged are punishable up to 7 years imprisonment.
It was also submitted that applicants undertake to co-operate during trial and they would appear as and when required by the investigating agency or Court.
It has been stated that in case, applicants are granted anticipatory bail, they shall not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate with the investigation and would obey all conditions of bail.
4. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has opposed the application for anticipatory bail.
5. As per first information report, the allegation is that the applicant induced the first informant to purchase a plot and consideration amount of Rs.7,00,000/- was fixed.

Out of which, two cheques were issued in the name of Asma of Rs.2,00,000/- each bearing cheque Nos.649749 dated 13.12.2021 and 469749 dated 13.12.2021 were fradulently withdrawn by the applicant no.1.
The maximum punishment, which can be awarded on conviction for the offences as alleged is 7 years and the applicants are having no criminal history.

6. It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
7. In the instant case, considering the settled principle of law regarding anticipatory bail,
submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, role of applicants and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merits, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
8. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.
